first_impression.reaction: We Googled this expecting a listicle of apps with affiliate links. Instead the first paragraph describes our actual guest list: family in Perth, friends in London, a colleague in Singapore, all telling us different flight times. That earns the scroll. No 'dream day' rubbish, and the takeaways box let us skim before deciding to read properly.

journey.quote: It is where your aunt in Perth, your school friends in London and your colleague in Singapore all tell you the same things: whether they are coming, which nights they will be there, what they eat and when their flight lands.
journey.reaction: That's literally our guest list. Half our people are flying in, so 'which nights they will be there' is the bit we hadn't thought about yet.

journey.section: The five kinds of wedding RSVP website compared
journey.quote: There is no single right tool, only the right kind for your guest list, judged on what a destination weekend asks of it.
journey.reaction: Fine, no platform names, which is a bit annoying because we'll have to go and find them ourselves. But the table with a 'Trade-off' column is honest and quick to scan. Good enough to send to James.

journey.quote: Wonderland Studio, our planning app for seating charts and RSVPs, sits in this group.
journey.reaction: At least they say it's theirs instead of pretending to be neutral. It doesn't oversell it, so it doesn't bother us.

journey.section: What changes between paid tiers and those at no cost
journey.quote: If the answers that matter sit behind a paid tier, upgrade early rather than rebuild halfway through.
journey.reaction: Practical. That's the kind of thing you learn the hard way at month nine. The checklist is the most useful part for us right now.

journey.quote: A guest may be at the ceremony but land too late for the welcome dinner, and your numbers for each event should show it.
journey.reaction: This is the insider detail we look for. Someone who has actually counted heads for a welcome dinner wrote that.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, so these answers have somewhere useful to go.
journey.reaction: It's dropped in mid-section and reads like an ad break. 'Somewhere useful to go' is vague. Does the advisor take our arrival list and sort the airport transfers for my grandparents, or do we still do it? It doesn't say.

journey.quote: When guests live in other countries, write your reply date with a date and a time zone, so nobody in another time zone misses it by a day.
journey.reaction: Small but real. My cousins in London would absolutely miss it by a day.

journey.section: Guest privacy and who can see the site
journey.quote: As general information as at November 2026, and not legal advice: personal information includes information or an opinion that could identify an individual, depending on whether that person is identifiable in the circumstances.
journey.reaction: As a lawyer I appreciate that it's dated, sourced and caveated properly. Slightly heavy for a wedding blog, but the plain advice at the end of the section is what we'll actually use.

journey.section: Guest privacy and who can see the site
journey.quote: Weighing several events, room blocks and a guest list across time zones? Talk to our [Wedded Concierge] team about the weekend you have in mind.
journey.reaction: Not a hard sell, but it lands straight after the Privacy Act paragraph, which is an odd moment to be pitched. It would make more sense after the bit about exporting numbers for the venue.

journey.section: QR code RSVPs and when to print the link too
journey.quote: So print the RSVP web address beside the code, short and easy to type, for guests who would rather not scan.
journey.reaction: Yes. Half of James's family won't scan a QR code. Good, specific advice.

journey.section: Plan the weekend, not just the replies
journey.quote: Turning them into a weekend where every guest is looked after is where a Wedded Advisor comes in: one Wedded Advisor, start to finish, as a single point of contact.
journey.reaction: Every planner says 'start to finish'. What does that actually cover? The article already told us earlier (venue, travel, vendors, payments) but this closing line goes generic again right when we'd be deciding.

unanswered_questions: Which actual tools fall into each of the five kinds? We'll have to research names ourselves.
Does our Wedded Advisor use the arrival and departure dates from our RSVPs to organise airport transfers and room blocks, or do we still manage that ourselves?
Does a Wedded Advisor set up or manage the RSVP website for us, or is that always on the couple?
Is Wonderland Studio something we pay for separately, or is it included if we work with Wedded Wonderland?
What does working with a Wedded Advisor cost, even as a range?
Are there real weddings where you ran a multi-event weekend with guests from several countries?

cta_reaction.quote: Start the conversation with our [Wedded Concierge] team.
cta_reaction.why: The tone is calm and we like that it isn't pushy. But this is one practical post, we haven't chosen a destination, and we haven't seen a real wedding from them yet. We'd read two more posts and look for a real multi-event wedding before enquiring. A closing line that says concretely what the advisor handles would move this closer to a yes.

top_3_changes: Make the closing advisor line concrete using what the article already says. Old: "Turning them into a weekend where every guest is looked after is where a Wedded Advisor comes in: one Wedded Advisor, start to finish, as a single point of contact." New: "Turning them into a weekend where every guest is looked after is where a Wedded Advisor comes in: one Wedded Advisor, start to finish, as a single point of contact for venue, travel, vendors and payments."

Tie the mid-section advisor line to the specific answers instead of 'somewhere useful'. Old: "Your Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, so these answers have somewhere useful to go." New: "Your Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, so arrival dates and room requests are answers you can pass straight to them."

Move the primary CTA so it doesn't follow the Privacy Act paragraph. Cut the line beginning "Weighing several events, room blocks and a guest list across time zones? Talk to our [Wedded Concierge]" (unchanged, including its utm_content=primary link) from the end of 'Guest privacy and who can see the site' and place it, word for word, at the end of 'Exporting numbers for your venue and caterer', after "...is a useful read."
